blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Typed e-mail address written to the log platform through the error message) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (Chat vendor receives phone, birth date, address and e-mail when greeting needs a name) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: throw new NotFoundError(`no customer with e-mail ${email}`);
findings.recommendation: Keep the e-mail address out of the error message (for example `throw new NotFoundError("no customer for this e-mail")`). Every lookup that misses reaches `errorHandler` (src/server.ts:14), which runs `logger.error("request failed", { path: req.path, error: err.message })`, and the logger ships each line to the log platform. Each failed support search therefore stores the searched person's e-mail address in the logs (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) minimisation, Art. 32), including addresses of people who are not customers or were mistyped.
findings.title: Typed e-mail address written to the log platform through the error message

findings.evidence:
user: {
  id: String(customer.id),
  name: customer.name,
  email: customer.email,
  phone: customer.phone,
  birthDate: customer.birth_date,
  address: customer.address,
},
findings.recommendation: Send Helply only what the stated purpose needs — the proposal says the widget "greets the signed-in customer by name, so that the agent knows who they talk to": an opaque id and the name. Drop `email`, `phone`, `birthDate` and `address` from the widget settings (and from the `customerById` select if nothing else uses them). As written, every signed-in customer who loads `/chat/settings` hands their phone number, date of birth and postal address to the third-party chat processor (GDPR Art. 5(1)(b)-(c), Art. 25, Art. 28).
findings.title: Chat vendor receives phone, birth date, address and e-mail when greeting needs a name

findings.evidence: "SELECT id, email, name, phone, birth_date, address FROM customers WHERE lower(email) = lower($1)",
findings.recommendation: The proposal says only "Agents look a customer up by e-mail address.", without saying which fields an agent needs. Confirm with the team which fields the support screen uses and select only those; birth date and postal address are likely beyond the purpose (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c)). Confidence low: the support front-end that consumes this endpoint is not visible.
findings.title: Support lookup returns birth date, phone and address with no stated need

findings.evidence: - [x] personal-data — customers' records are read and the chat vendor receives who is chatting
findings.recommendation: A question for the team: record Helply as a processor (data processing agreement, GDPR Art. 28, record of processing Art. 30) and state where it hosts the data — if outside the EEA, the Chapter V transfer mechanism. Only the controller can confirm what was decided.
findings.title: Helply processor and its location not identified in the plan

findings.recommendation: The message reaches the logs through `errorHandler` (src/server.ts:14); the customer identifier is personal data. Drop the id from the message, or log it deliberately as a structured field if operations need it.
findings.title: Customer id written to the log platform on a missing record
